profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI, known as Ai2, is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The site notes partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud in support of open AI model development and scientific research platforms.

Ai2 applies its research across several domains, including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. Two AI products are tracked for the organization: OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs with a nonprofit research focus.

No litigation, SEC filings, patent records, or MCP server registrations are held for Ai2 in the current facts.
